levelMapping: Software Engineer = IC2 (0-4 YOE, ~Google L3-L4); Senior Software Engineer = IC3 (~Google L4-L5 band; Blind consensus pegs LinkedIn Senior ≈ Google L4 / 'FAANG SDE-2'). In India there is effectively no separate SDE-2 title: insiders say IC3 covers the SDE-2/SDE-3 range and at least one Bengaluru org has a hard 5-YOE minimum for IC3, though 3.5-4.5 YOE candidates do get SSE loops and offers. At 3.3 YOE expect the SE (IC2) ladder or a stretch SSE loop; LinkedIn routinely down-levels automatically (interviewers score every candidate and will offer SE if you interview for SSE but miss the senior bar), and a Dec-2024 SSE reject was told 'good for high-level SDE2 but not SDE3'. Confirm the level and whether a concurrency round is in your loop with the recruiter.

process.summary: Recruiter screen, then an eliminatory 45-60 min technical phone screen (CoderPad, often with CS-fundamentals quizzing before 1-2 coding questions), then a virtual onsite of 5-6 one-hour rounds: two DSA coding rounds (two questions each, drawn heavily from a small reused LinkedIn-tagged LeetCode bank with follow-up extensions), one system design (HLD), one 'technical communication' project deep-dive, and a hiring-manager round LinkedIn calls 'host manager', which is part behavioral and usually includes a 10-15 min mini design question. Systems & Infrastructure loops replace or add a dedicated concurrency round where working multithreaded code is expected (often in Java). Since late 2025/2026 many loops (US first, spreading) swap one coding round for an AI-assisted coding round on CoderPad (GPT/Gemini/Claude available) or HackerRank-with-AI: you must state the algorithm yourself, use the AI to implement, and are judged on how you review/test AI output and how many of a ladder of tasks you complete. Every round is scored on a four-point hire scale; mixed verdicts trigger an extra tie-breaker round rather than rejection.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, role bucket (Apps vs Systems & Infra), location, compensation expectations, why LinkedIn; recruiter may probe for concurrency/distributed-systems experience for infra reqs.
rounds.probes: Ask which track (Apps or Infra) you are in, whether your loop has a concurrency round and/or an AI-assisted coding round, and the expected language (infra concurrency rounds have assumed Java without telling candidates).

rounds.name: Technical phone screen
rounds.what: CoderPad, sometimes two interviewers. Intro + CS fundamentals (OS: paging/thrashing/mutex-vs-semaphore, networking: TCP vs UDP, core Java: final/finally/finalize/GC, DBMS/ACID, caching) followed by 1-2 LeetCode-style questions from the LinkedIn bank (Nested List Weight Sum I/II, Bulb Switcher, Max Stack, Valid Parentheses, Shortest Word Distance II, Paint House II, moving-average-of-stream are all reported screens). Eliminatory; result often same/next day.
rounds.probes: Optimal solution expected quickly; interviewers dry-run your code on inputs and dislike library shortcuts (one 2025 Bengaluru reject was for using substring() instead of implementing the logic). Follow-up extension almost always comes.

rounds.name: Online assessment (early-career/intern only)
rounds.what: HackerRank, 4 problems, LC easy-medium (reported: Paint House variant, modular exponentiation, bit-manipulation, longest-substring variant). Experienced hires normally skip the OA and get the live phone screen instead.
rounds.probes: Pass all test cases; speed matters.

rounds.name: Coding round 1 (DSA)
rounds.what: Two questions, usually one medium + one medium-hard, straight from the LinkedIn-tagged bank, often story-reskinned (seats in a cinema = Can Place Flowers; influencer matrix = Find the Celebrity; connection degrees = BFS).
rounds.probes: Expect a planned extension: islands → max area, tree → graph version, O(1) data structure → duplicates allowed, window → wrap-around string. Complexity analysis (average vs worst case) is pushed hard.

rounds.name: Coding round 2 (DSA)
rounds.what: Same format; 'medium + hard in one hour' is a common complaint. Trees/graphs, sliding window, heaps/top-k, and design-a-data-structure dominate.
rounds.probes: Code must actually run/dry-run clean; several candidates report writing their own test cases and being judged on edge-case handling more than on problem difficulty.

rounds.name: AI-assisted coding (2025-26, many loops)
rounds.what: CoderPad with built-in AI assistants (candidate picks GPT/Gemini/Claude) or HackerRank with an AI helper. A ladder of 3-4 incremental tasks on one artifact, e.g. LRU cache → add TTL → thread-safety, or debug a half-implemented maze class then generate a maze with a guaranteed path. You must devise the algorithm yourself; AI is for implementation.
rounds.probes: Why you accepted/rejected an AI suggestion, how you would test each change, what you would change for production (service boundaries, concurrency). Candidates are graded on tasks completed — one Aug-2026 reject was told he finished only 2 of 4 tasks. Reviewing AI output line-by-line for bugs (stale map updates on eviction, undefined variables) is the real test.

rounds.name: System design (HLD)
rounds.what: One prompt, infra-flavoured for Systems & Infra loops (metrics platform, top-k heavy hitters, KV store, job scheduler) and product-flavoured for Apps (calendar, typeahead, feed, notifications). Mid-level candidates get a scoped component; seniors get end-to-end with capacity estimates and failure handling.
rounds.probes: Interviewers interrupt frequently between decisions; API design, schema design and even writing a SQL query are reported inside this round (calendar design). Time-window aggregation, hot keys/skewed fan-out, Kafka usage and storage choice are recurring probes.

rounds.name: Technical communication
rounds.what: Deep dive into one past project you owned: business problem, your role vs the team's, architecture, trade-offs, rejected alternatives, production issues, measured outcome. Scored like a technical round; sometimes framed as 'explain it to me like I'm a new joiner/intern'.
rounds.probes: Several layers of cross-questioning on every design choice; candidates from small-scale/startup backgrounds report being marked down on scale, so pick your highest-scale story.

rounds.name: Hiring manager ('host manager' / 'host leader')
rounds.what: Billed as behavioral but largely technical: current project impact/cost/scale, why leaving, why LinkedIn, mentoring/leading, conflict and feedback stories mapped to LinkedIn values — plus, very often, a 5-15 min design question (internal notification system, catalog events at huge scale, job scheduler, fake/malicious post detection).
rounds.probes: Outcome-oriented follow-ups after every story ('what actually happened?'); operational-excellence and reusable-improvement examples; team-lead scenarios for senior candidates.

rounds.name: Craftsmanship (staff level; occasionally senior)
rounds.what: 8-10 scenario questions on engineering quality: code-review strategy, keeping quality high with many juniors, rescuing a legacy app with no tests/monitoring, prioritising bugs vs tests vs monitoring vs performance, measuring a service's success, mentorship principles, LinkedIn-values questions.
rounds.probes: Concrete examples required for every answer; not asked in most SE/SSE Bengaluru loops but appears at Staff and in some US senior loops.

process.indiaNotes: Bengaluru hires SE (IC2) and SSE (IC3); loops are virtual, 1-hour rounds, sometimes all in one day (a 2024 candidate had 4 technical rounds back-to-back with one 30-min break) and sometimes spread 1-2 days apart over ~2 weeks. India-specific flavour: (1) CS-fundamentals quizzing (OS/networking/Java/DBMS) inside the phone screen is near-universal; (2) Systems & Infrastructure loops in Bengaluru have a dedicated concurrency round (delayed scheduler, bounded blocking queue, producer-consumer) where working code is expected and Java is often silently assumed — Python answers have cost candidates the round; (3) the AI-assisted round was still mostly a US report through mid-2026 but is appearing in India loops — ask your recruiter; (4) level inflation is real: LinkedIn SSE India maps to strong SDE-2 elsewhere, postings say 5+ YOE but 3.5-4.5 YOE candidates clear it; at 3.3 YOE expect SE or an auto-down-level path from an SSE loop. Compensation data points: SE Bengaluru ~2.8 YOE offer (Feb 2024); SSE Bengaluru offers 45L base + $120k RSU (Oct 2024, 4 YOE) and 61L base + $182k RSU (8 YOE).
process.timeline: 2 weeks to ~6 weeks end-to-end once the recruiter engages; phone screen ~1-2 weeks after first contact, onsite ~1-3 weeks later (scheduling the panel is the slow step; multiple reschedules are commonly reported), verdict 3 days-1.5 weeks after the last round. Mixed feedback triggers an extra round instead of a decision.
tips: Grind the LinkedIn-tagged LeetCode list — multiple offer-holders say onsite questions came verbatim from it; the bank is small and heavily reused (Find Leaves, Celebrity, Nested List Weight Sum, Max Consecutive Ones III, Word Ladder, Max Stack, Insert/Delete/GetRandom, K-pairs/top-k, Paint House, Exclusive Time).
Prepare the planned extension for every bank problem: tree→graph, wrap-around string, duplicates allowed, circular variant, 'what if it doesn't fit in memory', average-vs-worst-case complexity.
Treat coding rounds as 'code must run': dry-run on the interviewer's test inputs, write your own test cases, handle edge cases, avoid built-in shortcuts that bypass the intended logic.

For infra loops, drill concurrency in Java: delayed scheduler, bounded blocking queue, producer-consumer with shutdown, semaphores/locks/context-switch questions (Defog Tech playlist, Baeldung, LC concurrency tag are the community-recommended prep). Confirm language expectations beforehand.

For the AI-assisted round: state your algorithm before touching the AI, review generated code line-by-line (eviction/state bugs are planted or common), narrate why you accept or reject suggestions, and watch the clock — completion count is scored.
Prepare one high-scale project story to production depth for technical communication; every behavioral answer should end with a measurable outcome.
Expect SQL/schema questions inside system design (calendar/meeting-scheduler prompts) — practice writing one real query.
System design: lead with time-window aggregation patterns (top-k over sliding windows, metrics rollups) for infra loops; hybrid fan-out and hot-key handling for feed/graph prompts.
process.notes: No classic OOD/machine-coding (parking lot) round for this band — the 'lld' list below holds the concurrency round (working multithreaded code, LinkedIn's de-facto LLD round in India infra loops) and the AI-assisted practical tasks. Platform: CoderPad for live rounds (HackerRank for intern/early-career OA and some AI rounds); no HireVue/CodeSignal reported. Two interviewers per room (one shadowing) is common. Four-point scoring per round; 'when in doubt, add a round'. Rejections commonly cite the concurrency round, the HM round, or system-design structure rather than DSA. 1point3acres threads (login-walled) corroborate the AI-CoderPad round existing through 2026 including reports of the AI extension itself failing mid-interview.

dsa.title: Find Leaves of Binary Tree
dsa.variant: LinkedIn's single most reused onsite question. Variants: N-ary tree version; 'order in which nodes fall off' with a TreeNode.children() starter interface; follow-up 'what if the input is a directed graph instead of a tree?' (2024 and Aug-2026 reports); asked as the closer when time is short.
dsa.evidence: Reported in 8+ loops: Sept 2025 Bengaluru Apps, 2023 SSE Bangalore, 2024 SSE infra reject (graph ext), 2022 SWE infra offer, ~2025 SWE 6957300, Nov 2024 US final round (falling-leaves form), Mar 2025 staff follow-up onsite, Aug 2026 PracHub (graph follow-up)

dsa.title: Find the Celebrity
dsa.variant: Often given as an n×n 'who follows whom' matrix: find the influencer followed by everyone who follows no one. Follow-ups: solve with no extra space (stack solution rejected), minimize knows() calls.
dsa.evidence: 6+ reports: IC2 2025 coding R1, SSE infra Feb 2025 onsite R1, SDE infra ~Oct 2025 R1, SSE 2022 onsite, Nov 2024 US final (matrix form), SSE Backend Oct 2024 tie-breaker round, Glassdoor Bengaluru SSE Sep 2024

dsa.title: Max Consecutive Ones III
dsa.variant: Follow-ups reported: wrap-around (circular array) version; multiple incremental constraint changes in one sitting; reworded statements that are 'almost the same'.
dsa.evidence: 5 reports: Sept 2025 Bengaluru coding R2, SSE infra Feb 2025 R4, SSE Backend Oct 2024 DSA2, SWE ~2025 (wrap-around follow-up), Nov 2024 US final

dsa.title: Nested List Weight Sum
dsa.variant: Phone-screen staple; sometimes given as a string like "[1[2,[3,4]]]" to parse and sum with depth weights, with a follow-up to use no extra space beyond recursion.
dsa.evidence: IC2 2025 phone screen; SSE Backend Oct 2024 screening (string form); community-known classic

dsa.title: Nested List Weight Sum II
dsa.variant: Depth-reversed weights. Key probe: do it in ONE traversal without precomputing max depth (two-pass answers get rejected; the running-sum re-add trick is expected). Asked in phone screens and tech screens.
dsa.evidence: 4 reports: Sept 2025 Bengaluru phone screen (one-pass demanded), SDE infra ~Oct 2025 screen, SSE 2022 phone screen, Nov 2024 US tech screen

dsa.title: Exclusive Time of Functions
dsa.variant: LinkedIn's version asks for BOTH inclusive and exclusive time of a given function from START/END log lines with nesting; interviewer expects a pure stack solution. Reported as 'medium-hard, not exactly on LeetCode'.
dsa.evidence: Sept 2025 Bengaluru coding R1 (hardest question of the loop per candidate); 2022 SSE Bangalore R1; Hello Interview question bank lists it asked at LinkedIn Senior in Oct and Nov 2025

dsa.title: Max Stack
dsa.variant: Asked in screens even at Staff level; expected to discuss 2-3 approaches (two stacks vs doubly-linked-list + TreeMap), code all helper methods and dry-run a test case.
dsa.evidence: Staff Bengaluru June 2025 screening (strong hire); 2024 SSE infra reject Coding-I; #3 in the July-2026 LC tag snapshot

dsa.title: Word Ladder
dsa.variant: Bidirectional BFS is the expected optimization; appears reworded ('shortest transformation sequence between two words in a dictionary'). Variants reported without further detail.
dsa.evidence: Staff June 2025 DSA2; SDE infra ~Oct 2025 R2 (variant); Glassdoor SWE Aug 2026 review; a 2025 SSE report describes 'a medium bidirectional BFS problem'

dsa.title: Shortest Word Distance II
dsa.variant: Follow-up: when one word is much rarer than the other, binary-search the frequent word's index list instead of the two-pointer merge.
dsa.evidence: Staff June 2025 DSA2 (binary-search extension); SWE ~2025 phone screen; #5 in July-2026 tag snapshot

dsa.title: Minimum Window Substring
dsa.variant: Staff variant: the source string wraps around (circular). Also appears as 'minimum length substring' in IC2 loops and paired with Max Consecutive Ones III in a two-pointer themed round.
dsa.evidence: Staff June 2025 DSA1 (wrap-around); SSE Backend Oct 2024 DSA2; IC2 Sep 2026 R1

dsa.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
dsa.variant: Standard follow-up: duplicates allowed (LC 381). Also probed: what does 'average O(1)' mean with duplicates; weighted random pick extension pushes toward binary search.
dsa.evidence: 4 reports: 2023 SSE Bangalore Coding-1, 2022 Systems&Infra onsite, 2022 SSE onsite (variation), phone-screen follow-up to All O'one in Feb 2025 SSE loop

dsa.title: All O`one Data Structure
dsa.variant: Asked in phone screens with the duplicates-allowed GetRandom as follow-up; also in a staff follow-up onsite. An LFU-like structure was a Jul-2025 US staff phone screen.
dsa.evidence: SSE Systems&Infra Feb 2025 phone screen; SSE 2022 onsite R2; Staff Mar 2025 follow-up onsite; Glassdoor Staff Jul 2025 (LFU-like)

dsa.title: Degrees of connection: shortest path between two LinkedIn members
dsa.statement: Given an adjacency list of member connections plus a source and target member, return the connection distance (1st/2nd/3rd degree) and print one shortest path. Plain BFS is accepted but the interviewer asks for better: bidirectional BFS, then probes average-case vs worst-case complexity of each direction's frontier.
dsa.variant: Also framed as 'shortest path from a node to a target, print the path' in infra loops.
dsa.evidence: 3 reports: 2023 SSE Coding-2 (pushed from BFS to bidirectional BFS), Staff June 2025 DSA1, SSE Feb 2025 R4

dsa.title: K Closest Points to Origin
dsa.variant: Follow-up: K closest to an ARBITRARY query point, repeatedly — pushes toward preprocessing / approximate nearest-neighbour discussion.
dsa.evidence: SSE Systems Infra 2025 DSA1 (with ANN follow-up); SSE Nov 2024 onsite R1

dsa.title: Find K Closest Elements
dsa.variant: Expected: binary search on window boundary O(log(n-k)+k), with tie-break to the smaller value. Follow-ups: unsorted input (size-k heap), data too large for memory (chunking/indexing). BST version (Closest BST Value II, LC 272) asked in an older loop.
dsa.evidence: May 2026 coding R2 (PracHub, detailed follow-ups); SSE Feb 2025 onsite R1; BST version in a 2022 offer loop

dsa.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
dsa.variant: LinkedIn's favourite form is PRODUCTS, not sums: top-K (or K smallest) products of pairs from two sorted arrays — negatives make the heap bookkeeping tricky; the naive multiply-all answer is rejected and candidates are pushed past the plain priority-queue solution.
dsa.evidence: 4 reports: SSE Nov 2024 R2 (top-K products, time ran out), 2022 Systems&Infra Coding-2 (k smallest pair products, asked to beat the heap), Staff Mar 2025 coding round (sums form, LC hard)

dsa.title: Sliding Window Maximum
dsa.evidence: SSE Nov 2024 onsite R2 (paired with top-K products; interviewer extended time 15 min)

dsa.title: Number of Islands
dsa.variant: Usually reworded (connected land regions, connected-components story). Extensions: Max Area of Island (LC 695), count-islands as a screen question. #1 in the July-2026 tag snapshot.
dsa.evidence: 4 reports: IC2 2025 coding R1 (variation), 2024 SSE infra Coding-I (extended to Max Area), 2022 infra phone screen, 2022 SWE offer onsite (components variant), Glassdoor US screen Dec 2025

dsa.title: Course Schedule II
dsa.variant: Also appears as 'detect cyclic dependencies in an N-ary tree/graph' and as a well-known topological-sort graph problem in phone screens; 'order tree nodes so children come before parents' is the same peeling idea.
dsa.evidence: Sept 2025 Bengaluru coding R2; SDE infra ~Oct 2025 R1 (cycle detection); SSE ~2025 TPS (topo sort); 2022 SSE R2 (children-before-parents)

dsa.title: Paint House / Paint House II
dsa.variant: Asked as a pair: solve Paint House, then Paint House II (LC 265) with k colors in O(N*K) time / O(K) space (track two smallest). Story variant: 'color cakes so no two adjacent match' with a circular follow-up. Also an OA problem.
dsa.evidence: Sept 2025 Bengaluru coding R1 (I then II); 2022 SWE phone screen (II with optimization push); 2022 infra Coding-2 (circular cakes); HackerRank OA variant (2022 offer)

dsa.title: Maximum Subarray
dsa.variant: Asked unmodified in a phone screen (strong-hire verdict for clean Kadane + explanation). Maximum Product Subarray (LC 152) is in the same tag cluster.
dsa.evidence: SSE Nov 2024 phone screen

dsa.title: Bulb Switcher
dsa.variant: Phone-screen staple (perfect-squares insight). Follow-up seen in community prep: generalize to m ≤ n passes / arbitrary divisor sets.
dsa.evidence: IC2 2025 phone screen; SWE ~2025 phone screen

dsa.title: Can Place Flowers (seat-allocation reskin)
dsa.variant: Always story-framed at LinkedIn: cinema-hall / office seating — given occupied seats (1s) and a headcount, can everyone sit with no two people adjacent? Boundary conditions at row ends are the probe.
dsa.evidence: Dec 2024 SSE R1 (seat allocation boolean form); Sept 2025 Bengaluru phone screen (cinema hall)

dsa.title: Second Minimum Node in a Binary Tree (tournament tree)
dsa.variant: Framed as a 'tournament tree' (each parent = min of its two children, leaves distinct): find the second smallest value without scanning all nodes.
dsa.evidence: Dec 2024 SSE Bengaluru R1

dsa.title: Valid Parentheses
dsa.variant: Tech-screen warm-up; sometimes staged (one bracket type with a counter first, then three types, then 'why does the counter trick fail?').
dsa.evidence: Nov 2024 US tech screen; community prep lists the staged variant

dsa.title: House Robber I + II
dsa.variant: Phone screen: solve House Robber, then extend to the circular House Robber II (LC 213) in the last minutes.
dsa.evidence: 2024 SSE infra phone screen

dsa.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
dsa.variant: Count-the-subsets-summing-to-target variant asked in a 2022 loop; interviewers push for the optimized (memoized/bitmask) version over plain backtracking.
dsa.evidence: SWE-ML 2025 DSA round; 2022 SSE R2 (count form); a Oct 2024 backend DSA round had 'a backtracking problem with an optimization the candidate couldn't find'

dsa.title: LRU Cache (and extensions)
dsa.variant: Now the anchor of the AI-assisted round: implement LRU, then add TTL expiry, then thread-safety, as a graded task ladder. IC2 'AI + coding' variant: LRU with counters — predict and compute hit/miss ratios for given workloads. Also reported plain in an infra DSA round.
dsa.evidence: Aug 2026 AI-assisted round (4-task ladder, CoderPad+LLM); IC2 Sep 2026 AI round (counters/hit-ratio); SSE Systems Infra 2025 DSA1 (LRU-like)

dsa.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
dsa.variant: Elimination-round warm-up before a harder second question.
dsa.evidence: IC2 Sep 2026 elimination round

dsa.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
dsa.evidence: IC2 Sep 2026 elimination round (paired with Max Depth)

dsa.title: Max Points on a Line
dsa.variant: Slope-hashing with gcd normalization; watch verticals and duplicates.
dsa.evidence: 3 reports: IC2 2025 coding R2, SDE infra ~Oct 2025 R2, IC2 Sep 2026 R1 ('max collinear points')

dsa.title: Pow(x, n)
dsa.variant: Both recursive and iterative fast-power expected; the INT_MIN negation overflow is the planted edge case. Modular-exponentiation variant appeared in the HackerRank OA.
dsa.evidence: May 2026 coding R1 (PracHub, detailed); OA variant in a 2022 offer loop

dsa.title: Count distinct values in a huge sorted array
dsa.statement: A sorted array has n elements (n up to ~1 billion) but only k distinct values (k in the hundreds). Count the distinct values faster than a linear scan: binary-search the end of each run of equal values and jump block to block for O(k log n). Follow-up: analyze a divide-and-conquer version and identify its O(n) worst case when all values are distinct.
dsa.evidence: May 2026 coding R3 (PracHub)

dsa.title: Moving average of last N in a stream (excluding top K)
dsa.variant: Phone screen: average of the last N integers of an infinite stream; follow-up — same but excluding the top K of those N values (two-multiset / two-heap balancing), pseudo-code accepted for the follow-up.
dsa.evidence: 2023 SSE Bangalore phone screen

dsa.title: Convert an N-ary tree to a K-ary tree
dsa.statement: Rebuild an arbitrary N-ary tree as a K-ary tree in which every node has exactly 0 or K children, except at most one node which may have between 0 and K. Level-order traversal with queues to re-parent nodes is one accepted approach; preserving ordering while redistributing children is the tricky part.
dsa.evidence: 2023 SSE Bangalore Coding-1

dsa.title: Do two linked lists merge? (with cycles)
dsa.variant: LinkedIn's version adds cycles: acyclic lists intersect iff tails match; if either has a cycle both must, and a node of one cycle must lie on the other. Follow-ups: find each cycle and its entry point (Floyd).
dsa.evidence: SSE Systems Infra 2025 DSA2; 'a hard doubly-linked-list problem' also reported in a 2025 SSE onsite

dsa.title: Diameter of N-Ary Tree
dsa.variant: Also reported as 'a hard N-ary tree problem not on LeetCode or GFG' in another 2025 loop.
dsa.evidence: SSE Systems Infra 2025 DSA2

dsa.title: Binary Tree Upside Down
dsa.variant: Given with the 0-or-1-right-child constraint; interviewer threw a non-existent edge case to test whether the candidate would push back.
dsa.evidence: SWE ~2025 onsite R1

dsa.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
dsa.variant: Paired with Two Sum III – Data Structure Design (LC 170) in one phone screen, with a design-for-3Sum discussion follow-up.
dsa.evidence: Staff Mar 2025 technical phone screen

dsa.title: Two Sum III – Data Structure Design
dsa.variant: Follow-up: how would the design change for Three Sum (discussion only).
dsa.evidence: Staff Mar 2025 technical phone screen

dsa.title: Text Justification
dsa.variant: A 'coding + implementation' round on its own — correctness of the fiddly spacing rules is the whole test.
dsa.evidence: Staff Mar 2025 onsite coding round; long-standing LinkedIn bank member

dsa.title: Can the string become a palindrome under allowed edits?
dsa.variant: 2026 Apps onsite form: given a string and a set of allowed edits, determine whether it can be made a palindrome (generalization of Valid Palindrome II's delete-one-char).
dsa.evidence: SSE Apps 2026 onsite coding (Aced)

dsa.title: Most frequent ('popular') substring under constraints
dsa.statement: Find the most frequently occurring substring meeting given length constraints in a string. The interviewers rejected a solution built on String.substring()/built-ins and required re-implementing the windowing with a character-count hashmap, then dry-ran the code on several inputs.
dsa.evidence: SSE Productivity Engineering Bengaluru screen (~2021, re-posted guidance matches 2025 expectations); interviewers' no-built-ins stance corroborated by later reports

dsa.title: Graph Valid Tree
dsa.evidence: 2022 SSE Bangalore R1 (paired with the exclusive-time logs problem)

dsa.title: Accounts Merge
dsa.variant: Paired with a count-occurrences-of-pattern-string question where mentioning KMP (without full implementation) satisfied the interviewer.
dsa.evidence: 2022 SWE infra offer, onsite 3

dsa.title: Implement Rand10() Using Rand7() (rejection sampling)
dsa.variant: Asked in the AI/ML-engineer coding round with a mathematical-explanation-first expectation; backend candidates may see it as a probability warm-up.
dsa.evidence: SWE-ML 2025 AI coding round

dsa.title: Adapter over a KV store that only accepts 6-digit keys
dsa.statement: An existing key-value store API only accepts 6-digit keys. Design/implement a layer that supports keys of arbitrary size on top of it — hashing long keys down to 6 digits, handling collisions, and tracking mappings. Deliberately ambiguous between an algorithms and a design question; clarify scope early.
dsa.evidence: 2022 Systems & Infra Bangalore, solo-question round

design.title: Top-K heavy hitters over time windows (LinkedIn's signature design)
design.prompt: Design a system to surface the top K most-shared articles/posts/exceptions on LinkedIn over sliding windows (last 5 min, 1 hour, 24 hours). Variants: top third-party articles shared, top-K exceptions collected from many services over 24h, trending articles from a stream of shared URNs, top-K YouTube-style.
probes: bucketed/ring-buffer counting per time window and window merging
count-min sketch vs exact counts; memory trade-off
ingest pipeline: async processing, Kafka partitioning by URL/URN
hot keys and skew
caching, archival policy, analytics store
lambda vs streaming (real-time vs batch rollups)
design.evidence: 6+ reports: 2023 SSE (top articles), Nov 2024 SSE offer (top-K exceptions), Apr 2024 SSE offer (top N posts 5min/1h/24h), IC2 2025 (Top-K YouTube variation), Nov 2024 US final (top K shared posts), Staff Mar 2025 follow-up onsite (trending articles)

design.title: Metrics / observability platform
design.prompt: Design a system where thousands of services/machines publish metrics ([source, metric, value] tuples); store, aggregate, alert on thresholds, and serve dashboards. Variants: New Relic/Splunk-like logs+metrics platform; metric publishing system for CPU/memory of a distributed fleet.
probes: time-series storage, partitioning/sharding by host and time
query optimization by time range, host, and keyword
rollups/downsampling for month-long queries
alerting pipeline (e.g. email when CPU > 90%)
write-heavy ingest: Kafka, batching
interviewer interrupts between every decision — budget time
design.evidence: 5 reports: SDE infra ~Oct 2025 (metrics platform), 2024 SSE infra (metrics aggregation, 45 min felt too short), 2022 SSE (stats from hundreds of machines), 2022 SWE offer (metric publishing + alerting stretch), SSE Backend Oct 2024 (Splunk-like)

design.title: Distributed job / task scheduler

exactly-once vs at-least-once execution; retries and idempotency
worker health, leader election, failure handling
relationship to the concurrency-round DelayedScheduler (same idea, single-node code version)

design.title: Design a key-value store

replication and consistency levels

lld.title: Delayed task scheduler (concurrency)
lld.prompt: Implement a scheduler that accepts tasks with a delay and executes each when its delay elapses: schedule(task, delayMs), with worker thread(s) sleeping until the next due task. Working code expected, not pseudocode.
lld.deliverable: working multithreaded code (Java strongly preferred) + reasoning about locks/waits
probes: priority queue + condition-variable wait with re-check on new earlier task
thread pool sizing; what happens when a task is added that's due sooner than the current wait
locks vs semaphores; spurious wakeups
reported in ~6 of 10 Bengaluru infra concurrency rounds (candidate's own tally)
lld.round: Concurrency round (60 min, Systems & Infra loops)
lld.evidence: 2022 Systems&Infra Bangalore (with the 6/10 frequency claim); SWE Feb 2024 offer R4 ('standard LinkedIn concurrency question, hard follow-ups')

lld.title: Bounded blocking queue
lld.prompt: Design and implement a bounded blocking queue (producer-consumer): put() blocks when full, take() blocks when empty. Start with n writers/1 reader, extend to n writers/n readers.
lld.deliverable: working code with correct lock/semaphore usage; interviewer probes behavior of specific code changes
probes: semaphores vs ReentrantLock + two conditions vs wait/notify
which thread acquires the lock first on wakeup; context switches at each stage
deadlock traps when mixing synchronized blocks with semaphores
edge cases: shutdown, interrupts
lld.round: Concurrency round (60 min); also a 2025 Bengaluru HLD-adjacent round
lld.evidence: 4 reports: Apr 2024 SSE offer R4, 2022 SWE offer onsite 4, 2022 SSE round 4 (n-reader extension), Glassdoor Bengaluru Jun 2025 ('design a blocking queue with concurrency'); LC 1188 is the practice form

lld.title: Producer-consumer with graceful shutdown
lld.prompt: Implement producer-consumer with an explicit shutdown mechanism: producers/consumers drain or stop cleanly on shutdown signal without losing in-flight items or deadlocking.
lld.deliverable: working code; Java was silently expected (a Python solution hurt the candidate)
probes: context switches at each blocking point
which thread gets the lock when leaving the blocking queue
poison-pill vs flag+interrupt shutdown
lld.evidence: 2023 SSE Bangalore concurrency round (cited in the rejection)

lld.title: Thread-safe HashMap
lld.prompt: Design your own thread-safe hash map: bucketing, per-bucket locking vs global synchronization, resize strategy. Asked cold in a phone screen.
lld.deliverable: class design + code with synchronization; discussion of lock granularity
probes: coarse vs striped locking; why ConcurrentHashMap segments
correct equality semantics (a candidate was dinged for == on strings)
resize under concurrency
lld.evidence: 2022 SSE Bangalore telephone screen; 'concurrent hashmap' tallied as ~1 of 10 concurrency rounds in another report

lld.title: AI-assisted task ladder: LRU cache → TTL → thread-safe
lld.prompt: In the AI-assisted round (CoderPad with GPT/Gemini/Claude): implement an LRU cache, then extend with TTL expiry, then (task 4) thread safety — four graded tasks in ~60 min. You must state the algorithm (hashmap + doubly linked list) yourself; AI is only for implementation.
lld.deliverable: as many completed, reviewed, working tasks as possible; completion count is scored
probes: catching AI bugs: map not updated on eviction, undefined variables, incompatible snippets across generations
explaining why you accepted/rejected each AI suggestion
